Fix flaky tests rather than tolerate unrelated required Windows checks failing. ## What

Answer live reply envelopes when their notes are queued, so later edits proceed while notes retain receiver order. Receipts expose per-node note results; `status` shows queued inboxes and subsequent delivery or refusal without those receiver results rewriting outcomes. Processing failures receive refusals, and unwritten answers and remaining claimed envelopes stay pending for the same driver to retry.

## Why

Managers need to know promptly what applied and what is waiting. A worker’s hours-long turn should not make a reply look lost and prompt duplicate edits, adoption of a live run, or cancelled work.

## Additional info

Four Rust source-compatibility breaks: `CommandVerdict::Queued`, `Delivery::Queued` (re-exported by `views`), the public field `Receipt::notes`, and the public field `RunReading::inbox`. Consumers must handle the new variants and update struct literals or exhaustive destructuring. The planner-channel schema advances to 2.0.0; the events schema advances to 1.10.0 for the optional note index on `edit-rejected` records. The receipt’s `notes` key and status `inbox` are omitted when empty. Every other public-type change is a new type.

body.title: feat!: interrupt live turns with manager notes and bound or withdraw their delivery
body.body:
## What

Manager notes now interrupt the addressed worker or supervisor by default, with explicit `turn-end` delivery and outcomes that distinguish interruption from delivery at turn end. Optional delivery deadlines appear in status; expired notes are carried or refused according to `persist`.

Add `withdraw-note` for carried notes awaiting dispatch. Carried notes accumulate in order, and withdrawal removes only the selected note. Add admission-driven note journeys and recovery regressions, and reconcile the public types, schemas and contract documentation.

## Why

A manager’s correction must affect work underway without discarding the dispatch’s conversation or waiting hours for a turn to finish. Managers also need an accurate delivery outcome, a way to bound waiting, and a way to retract obsolete instructions before they are read.

## Additional info

Breaking Rust API change to `Command` and `Deliver`. Existing envelopes and records without `turn` remain readable; callers wanting non-interrupting live delivery should specify `deliver: "turn-end"`.

Live delivery falls back to turn-end delivery when interruption is unavailable, including on Windows. Configured deadlines still bound that wait.

Live withdrawal remains explicitly refused until oneagentgraph supports withdrawing an offer while delivery waits on it. The refusal leaves delivery and the original note’s outcome unchanged; the interim rule is documented in contract-divergences entry 133.

Closes nickderobertis/ai-orchestrator#1902, nickderobertis/ai-orchestrator#1622, nickderobertis/ai-orchestrator#1834, and #512.

## What

Reduce redundant git process starts during busy review rounds by throttling session-close checks, avoiding unnecessary release lookups, and reading independent landings concurrently. ## Why

Repeated repository reads amplify Windows process-start costs, pushing the busy review round past its 540-second bound. ## What

Adopt oneharness-core 0.28.5 and oneagentgraph 0.5.14 so concurrent judged Codex dispatches share one app-server. Add a real linked-dispatch regression journey with coverage-safe server counting, macOS-safe socket paths, durable sweeper evidence, and protocol checks for the recording Codex double.

Merge main’s fixes and correct retained-driver claim detection on Windows, including after the child exits.

## Why

Sharing one app-server per configuration prevents concurrent Codex turns from each starting their own server. These engine dependencies enable that behavior for hosts; the regression fixes address the checks blocking adoption.

## Additional info

The pool and its sweeper run in the real `oneharness` subprocess launched by onejudge. `onepipeline`, the only binary this repository ships, does not lease pooled servers itself: its in-process, single-sided turns use `codex exec`.

Windows previously returned no start token for an exited child, allowing a PID match to accept another process’s recorded start. Claim confirmation now reads creation time through the retained child handle and rejects a recorded start when the child’s start cannot be read.

Retain onejudge 0.19.5 and one resolved copy of each engine. That release carries the sweeper and satisfies oneagentgraph’s requirement; adopting onejudge 0.20.0 would introduce a second copy for an unrelated breaking change.

## What

Move plan-store items to `done` when a landing closes their GitHub issues, using the existing store configuration with no new setting. Deduplicate by landing commit, catch up on adoption and late merges, and support `publish-branch`, `repo-recover` and `integrate`.

Journal results as `landing-closures`; retry transient failures without blocking scheduling and surface failures without changing node settlement or command exit status. Landing verbs also retry transient operation-stream reads so closure reports are not lost.

## Why

Closed follow-up issues still appeared as open board work and were selected again by agents. Passing the landing’s closed issues directly to the store keeps configured boards current without scanning whole boards or spending requests on landings that close nothing. The store decides which configured sources’ items move.

## Additional info

BREAKING CHANGE: Upgrade the linked `onetaskgraph` family to 0.8.0, affecting producer types exposed through the public plan and store APIs. Copy requests gain status filtering and skipped results, store failures gain `statuses-not-tasks`, and closed-item status names follow the closure reason, including `cancelled` for duplicates. Upgrade `onevcs` to 0.56.2 and `onevcs-testing` to 0.19.12 to consume landing closure reports. The events schema advances to 1.8.0 with the new `landing-closures` record.

Adapt cancellation journeys to the linked producer’s interruptible pushes and fix test synchronization exposed on Windows: closure reporting can precede settlement, and newer Git versions can create `origin/HEAD` during fetch. body.title: fix: hold live notes per receiver and never hold findings behind them
body.body:
## What

Deliver live manager notes concurrently per receiver, releasing each node’s hold as it answers while preserving ordering through earlier held envelopes. Unrelated edits and findings can proceed; mixed envelopes commit non-note commands at handoff and report per-command outcomes if a note is later refused.

Human and JSON status distinguish active delivery, held envelopes, and unanswered work awaiting the next driver.

## Why

One busy worker could stall unrelated corrections and findings for hours while status made its pending note look abandoned. Managers need updates to move as fast as their receivers allow and accurate status to distinguish a slow worker from a lost message.

## Additional info

Closes #1011, #801, #803, #754.

## What

Size the two-source journey’s settlement wait to the plan’s longest dependency chain, allowing one harness step per sequential dispatch. ## Why

The contract says “a node — and each step within a lifecycle node — dispatches the moment its dependencies settle `done`.” That establishes sequential execution along the chain; it specifies no dispatch deadline. body.title: fix(continuation): never dispatch a node the displaced driver settled
body.body:
## What

Keep a published node fenced until its settlement reaches the shared store, and defer takeover acknowledgement until then—even after the displaced driver's bounded wait expires. The adopting host continues the published node and dispatches only its unfinished dependants. Two controlled-hold regression journeys cover reads before settlement persistence and persistence delayed beyond that wait.

## Why

A host taking over a stored project must not redo work another host already published. This race caused intermittent double dispatch and failed main's required Windows merge check, preventing correct changes from reliably completing their merge path.

## Additional info

In `src/engine.rs`, `converge` previously removed the publication fence on `Message::Settled`, before asynchronous write-back persisted the settlement. Its superseded-driver path could also acknowledge after a bounded wait without confirming persistence. Either let the adopter read a project missing the settlement and dispatch the node again.

[Contract-divergences entry 128](docs/contract-divergences.md) promises that “what the displaced driver settled while it was being taken over is continued rather than dispatched again”. Entry 129 records the proposed changes to the conflicting timing rules; the existing journey's assertion remains unchanged.

Refused-projection retry rules remain unchanged. If the store refuses a settlement and the graph never changes, takeover can remain blocked until the fence is cleared or the displaced host's records prove the run gone. Resolving that case is deferred to a follow-up.

body.title: fix(scratch): record a retained dispatch's scratch path as the dispatch was given it on Windows
body.body:
## What

Add regression coverage requiring dispatch scratch paths and `scratch-retained` paths to match as text, preserving the existing paused-run journey’s assertion. The engine path fix is already on main through [#977](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/pull/977).

Keep departing drivers from attempting observer restarts after release while still reporting stopped observers. Cover attached and detached adoption, and wait for ownership release before repairing a legacy launch record.

## Why

The Windows scratch journey blocks the required cross-platform check and therefore every change request’s merge path, including [#904](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/pull/904). Removing that blocker lets releases carry the Codex plugins-off and shared app-server work from [oneharness#1442](https://github.com/nickderobertis/oneharness/pull/1442). The driver changes protect adoption and record repairs from departing drivers.

## Additional info

The [original failing Windows job](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38887444753/job/116928910996) prints the failed assertion but neither path value. The diagnosis rests on the pre-fix allocator returning `canonicalize` unchanged while the retained-record producer removes the Windows `\\?\` prefix: two spellings of the same directory. The engine was wrong; the journey’s comparison remains unchanged. Main’s #977 now derives both paths from the same scratch root. Main’s [#1003](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/pull/1003) supplies the protection against stale launch-record writes; this diff adds release-time observer reporting and adoption coverage on top.

The scratch journey passed on [Windows](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38983520867/job/117249655817) and [macOS](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38983520867/job/117249655797) in run **38983520867**, and again on [Windows in run 38998427985](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38998427985/job/117296053473) and [run 39013380285](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/39013380285/job/117340453845). The [Linux gate in run 38983520867](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38983520867/job/117249590951) passed without listing individual tests; the journey also passed locally.

On the finished tree, **203 selected tests passed**, covering every scratch and driver e2e journey and the engine, driver, executor and scratch unit tests. Formatting, Clippy with warnings denied, and diff-scoped llmlint passed. This supersedes the earlier 201-test result; the earlier prefix-stripping test and [CI diff-scoped llmlint](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38983520867/job/117249591126) also passed. The full local gate was not run, as requested.

The Windows-only unit regression directly checks the verbatim-prefix cause, but the inspected Windows jobs stopped before unit tests; its pre-fix failure is inferred from the code, not observed. The cross-platform text-equality test passes on both the finished tree and the original base on Linux, where the Windows spelling difference does not occur. A Linux mutation using `/tmp/…` versus `//tmp/…` demonstrated that it rejects differing text even when path-component equality accepts it.

Earlier CI blockers and their follow-up:

- Windows timed out after 180 minutes without test failures in runs **38983520867** and **38998427985**, completing 1236/1375 and 1083/1375 e2e tests respectively. The latter failed the [required Windows check](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38998427985/job/117331367669).
- Run **38967292257** encountered a [Windows summary-listing flake](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38967292257/job/117197542129), “only 1 reads ran against the writer, which is not a race”, and a [macOS restacking flake](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38967292257/job/117197542026), “the rework settled before the restack started”.
- Run **38998427985** encountered a [macOS linear-writeback flake](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38998427985/job/117296053534), “the loopback must refuse malformed requests before a valid run”, following `ValueError: unknown url type: '/graphql'`. It passed all three reruns, but fail-fast left 850 e2e tests unrun, including scratch.

The follow-up fixes landed in [#982](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/pull/982) and were merged into this branch. Empty commit `65efc3ad` was pushed afterward; [CI run 39136520073](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/39136520073) was queued at the last recorded check, so no final CI result is claimed.

body.title: fix(smoke): start the node above a settled stack within the continuation journey's bound
body.body:
## What

Make the continuation smoke journey hold only its intended node, so a stacked parent's retry can run. Separate publication settlement from dependent dispatch, derive the publication wait from onevcs's documented timings, and include both hosts' recorded state in timeout messages.

## Why

Correct work should pass the change request merge path. This journey proves that a cold host can take over a stored project and carry it forward; its own waits and turn holds must not prevent that progress.

## Additional info

The [failed smoke job](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/39076442278/job/117524508479) and the worker's GitHub inspection show that #1259 belonged to node `a`; `b` pushed its branch but never opened a change request. The retained log cannot distinguish a failed publication, a held retry, or a stalled GitHub call, so the exact incident cause remains unproven.

The journey did contain a reproducible deadlock: its global `turn.hold` also blocked a retried parent, while releasing that hold required its dependent to start. The contract says, “Every publication failure is named, and a preserving one is re-dispatched.” The new offline stacked-retry regression proves that the parent can retry and settle before its dependent starts; restoring the global hold makes it time out.

The settlement wait now allows onevcs's 120-second draft grace plus one 30-second checks poll, with a separately identified discretionary 30-second allowance for git/GitHub calls. This is a single-publication allowance, not the engine's full retry bound. Production publication settings remain in effect; a second dispatch or publication fails immediately with diagnostics.

The five added offline tests passed, including deterministic wait-bound and timeout-diagnostic tests. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied passed, and the smoke binary built. The credentialled smoke journey was not run because the required scratch-repository credential was unavailable.

## Why

## What

Consolidate macOS coverage into one sequential PR job and one pre-publication release job, preserving Linux/Windows coverage and protected check names. Semantic release-only PRs, base pushes and downstream smoke request no Mac runner; manual Mac diagnostics default off.

**Intel macOS artifacts are discontinued from the next release.** Apple Silicon retains archive, wheel and npm packaging with native install/smoke checks before publication.

## Why

The shared five-runner macOS pool spends several scarce slots on one change, leaving otherwise green work and dependent releases queued. Consolidating existing proofs and builds returns slots to other changes.

## Additional info

### Scheduling and release compatibility

Baseline: `bdd2b29578a0dcbb2236bb1f0516bc90e60f9692`. Finished head: `6fa78f1a95a5a0084ba535819e53fe4f5db84779`. It retains `c30c5dc70f648116f1b7487ab9f354a081427cc1`, merges main at `e28ee8eaefb1cc99a377d85ee11d48083f208fad` through `810345e0`, and subsequently merges main at `26a06e55` through `5dcbee94`.

The merged CI retains main’s Windows per-leg verdict and 220-minute job/180-minute cross-check limits. Both consolidated Mac proof jobs have the 180-minute cross-check limit and 240-minute job limits, leaving time for reruns and installs.

These counts describe **modelled workflow routes**, not observed runner executions. The contract interpreter expands actual matrices, evaluates Actions expressions, traverses the pinned reusable workflow and follows downstream triggers. Unsupported resolution fails explicitly.

| Workflow | Triggering events, before → after | Mac jobs/run before | Mac jobs/run after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ci.yml` | push, pull_request → push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch | 3: cross, install, install-documented | Ordinary PR: 1; semantic release-only PR and base push: 0; manual default: 0; opted-in diagnostic: 1, outside the lifecycle |
| `release.yml` | release → unchanged | 10: upload ×2, build-wheels ×2, build-npm ×2, verify-pypi ×2, verify-npm ×2; Apple Silicon and Intel, with Intel removed by this change | 1 Apple Silicon build/install job across publish-flag combinations |
| `published-smoke.yml` | workflow_run, workflow_dispatch → unchanged | 4: PyPI and npm on Apple Silicon and Intel, with Intel removed by this change | 0 |
| `engine-currency.yml` | push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch → unchanged | 0 | 0 |
| `notignored.yml` | pull_request → unchanged | 0 | 0 |
| `release-plz.yml` | push → unchanged | 0 | 0 |
| `release-sweep.yml` | pull_request → unchanged | 0 | 0 |
| `visual-docs.yml`, including pinned screencomp v0.4.8 reusable call | pull_request, push, schedule → unchanged | 0 | 0 |

| Release platform | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linux x86_64 | Archive + checksum, wheel + SBOM, npm package | Unchanged |
| Linux aarch64 | Archive + checksum, wheel + SBOM, npm package | Unchanged |
| Apple Silicon macOS | Archive + checksum, wheel + SBOM, npm package | Retained; built, installed and run natively in one job; release attachment and publication run on Linux |
| Intel macOS | `x86_64-apple-darwin` archive + checksum, Intel wheel + SBOM, `onepipeline-cli-darwin-x64` | **Removed from the next release** |
| Windows x86_64 | Archive + checksum, wheel + SBOM, npm package | Unchanged |

The launcher package and crates.io crate remain. Darwin packaging retains bundled helper executables, README, license, changelog, flat archive layout and checksum names. The npm launcher explicitly refuses Intel macOS and recommends building from source with `cargo install onepipeline --locked`; the packed-launcher test covers that refusal. `release-targets.toml` records the discontinued npm package as retired.

Recorded telemetry reports **1 Mac job/run** and **2 Mac-spending runs/change**, within both registered budgets. It covers twelve event classes, three diff classes, same-repository/fork ownership, publish combinations and lifecycles with and without a release PR. The uncached Nx workflow test records telemetry; SDK reporters read it and reject missing or stale records. Only the budget checker compares measurements with thresholds.

Each budget registration’s description records the approved exception: the brief requires both per-run and per-change ceilings, and both remain separate. One run can occupy several shared Mac slots even when the lifecycle count remains within its bound; the jobs/run description carries this `inner_measure_reason`. Neither registration has a separate rationale comment or a `budgets_track_product_owner_outcomes` marker because that rule is not configured here. Existing budget thresholds and lint rules are unchanged.

### Routing and required contexts

The shared semantic classifier authorizes Mac omission only for a same-repository `release-plz-` branch whose parsed diff changes versions/changelog alone. Author identity cannot authorize omission. Forks, forged or mixed release branches, registry dependency changes—including a dependency named `onepipeline`—and unreadable PR input require Mac coverage. They use `always()` and explicit prerequisite/per-leg outcomes, reject failed, cancelled or missing required work, and label authorized omissions without claiming tests ran. Proof jobs have distinct names. This branch does not edit branch protection; release-compat remains its separately selected tier.

The previous conditional matrices could leave rendered contexts unreported when the crate was unaffected, `changes` failed or `gate` prevented installation. The existing non-matrix `deny`, `msrv`, `smoke` and `release-compat` jobs retain their path-sensitive skips under their existing names. body.title: fix(test): end every process a test spawns before the test returns
body.body:
## What

Make shared test-fixture teardown terminate and wait for harness doubles and their descendants, with PID-based regression coverage. CI now fails and reruns tests that leak output handles; the leak-detection regression also waits for its own deliberately leaked processes to exit.

Raise the cross-platform gate’s timeout to 180 minutes and its job’s to 220 minutes. Give the readjust store journey 600 seconds and other Windows tests 540 seconds to accommodate the slower runner image; other platforms retain their existing limits. Prevent the maintenance failure fixture from repeating its command during the same phase on slow hosts.

## Why

Leftover processes keep the required Windows check’s output open after tests pass, forcing two-hour reruns and blocking correct changes. This repeatedly blocked #904’s fix for 30–50 GB of daily Codex plugin catalog downloads. Cleanup lets the check finish when its work ends; the increased limits give the existing test tiers time to complete.

## Additional info

Windows containment includes orphaned descendants. Unix cleanup covers processes still descended from the test at teardown and continues waiting for those it finds even if their parents exit; processes orphaned to init before teardown remain outside that guarantee.

The macOS regression assertion failed because a Linux-only `/proc` probe treated exited zombies as running. The probe now uses `ps`, and teardown accepts macOS’s unclassified `?` process states.

The leak-detection regression previously passed on Linux but was itself marked `LEAK-FAIL` on Windows because its inner runs’ sleepers inherited the outer test’s output handles. It now waits for their recorded PIDs to exit and asserts that none remain on every supported platform.

body.title: feat(views): name every skipped node and the dependency that skipped it
body.body:
## What

`results` reports each skipped node as never attempted and names the
dependencies that skipped it with their own statuses, and the run summary
carries `N never attempted` beside the done count.

`onepipeline attest RUN REFERENCE` now takes a node that settled `failed` as
well as a ready human action: the node stops gating, everything it had skipped
becomes ready inside the loop already running, and `results` shows it as
`settled failed, attested as landed` so a failure is never read as a success.
Any other settlement is refused naming both accepted references. This widens a
published contract and is recorded as open divergence 36, gated by an end-to-end
journey that drives the settlements out of the record itself.

`runs` and `status` print `OBSERVER DEAD` or `NO OBSERVER` beside the driver
word for an executing run, decided from the launch record's graph run, its
ending, and its owner lock rather than the process table; the detached driver
now reaps its observer so that lock can clear. The unread-surface line names the
kinds waiting beside the count and staleness, blocking first, then rarest, with
any remainder counted rather than cut.

Also fixes an end-to-end test that read the driver's log without waiting for it,
racing the driver's own poll and failing two of three macOS runs.

## Why

These are facts a run held but could not state. A skip is re-derived from its
dependency on every pass and the cause was discarded, so `11/27 done` said
nothing about which nodes were never tried or what stopped them — now the node
and the dependency are both named. Nor was there any answer to type when the
failed work had in fact landed: a node here stayed skipped for three days over a
change already merged, so attesting a failure as landed is what releases its
